title: Sashi Brown Full Media Availability at 2026 NFL Meetings | Baltimore Ravens
text: As far as your new head coach, Jesse Mentor. >> Yeah. >> Um, what was kind of for you the moment in that process that you kind of thought, >> you know, he he he could be the the the the next Ravens head coach? >> I don't know if there was any one point that it jumped out of me. It was just kind of strong from the start and stayed strong throughout. Uh, you know, our first impression was fantastic. Those guys had been here with Jess before, so talked a little about them. uh got a chance to you know do a little diligence talking to Oz and some of the guys in the building who have been with him but then when I got a chance to meet him on that first Zoom you know he's just very impressive clear thinker heard from a lot of people as I said at the press conference around the league unprompted like hey this is a real guy that you guys ought to look at and and Jess was impressive throughout the process in terms of the way that he approaches it alignment in terms of the way we want to go about things uh and the way we want to win and build our organization and roster and team play football. So, um just very consistently positive throughout the entire process. >> How how important was that? You mentioned the alignment. You know, you move on from a long-term head coach, but there's there's some thread there that you know connected with the organization before. It's not like you guys just rip things up and move a different direction. Yeah, we try to be incredibly thoughtful first and respectful of John and we challenged ourselves on that decision as you know which was not an easy decision as Steve shared. I think when we sat and talked with Jess, finding someone first of all really going into the process, I think understanding what we were looking for, what we needed and why, pushing on that quite a bit. We had a lot of good discussion internally, Azie, Eric, myself, Dick, Steve. So, when we we got to the point where we're having conversations with all candidates, including Jesse, we had a really good sense of what we were looking for. And that alignment, I think, is really important. So you can get into the interview phase. Uh, and there's a ton of just talented people out here that are vying for these jobs, but it's really important to know yourself and what you think will be important for your success long term. And Jess represented embodied a lot of that. >> Um, 101 minority matters just going through the process yourself. Now, what do you think we will do to move in the right direction? I think, you know, we're going to consistently take a look at the process, take a look at the pipeline, take a look at ourselves, uh, in terms of where we are. We had some incredible folks. I mean, surprised, but we'll also say we were really familiar with Jess, but also surprised uh, that Vance didn't get a look, and I think he will eventually. He's going to have that defense running again. Uh but you know ultimately we need you know more talented folks in the pipeline. We need to make sure the pipeline's identifying those folks and um that's going to be something that's going to be a point of emphasis for the league as we move forward. So you know we want our fan bases, our front offices, our coaching staffs to reflect our locker rooms, our communities. Uh and that's something that I said at my first press conference. We're behind on we need to get better at. What were some of those non-negotiables for the head coach? What were the head coach must be? >> Yeah, I think the first thing is always start with character for us. You know, we want someone who's got character as a human being. Uh but also football character, someone who's passionate about the sport, uh has a lot of respect for our community, is going to represent us well throughout the state, Baltimore. Uh and so that was really important to us. That's really kind of the first non-negotiable for us. We're going to bring in someone who's going to be a great teammate, great leader for organization, Justin's going to be the face of our franchise, we hope for a very long time. Uh so beyond the talent, which is also the other piece, you know, someone who's really a teacher and a great leader and an organizer of our football program. Uh that's the other piece, someone who's uh going to really embody what we're we're looking for in style of play, uh intensity, the ability to, you know, be creative and innovative as well. So we stay at the forefront of uh concepts and tactics and scheme uh but someone who's going to be a great partner to Eric as well. You know that partnership is incredibly important. So >> excuse me. I apologize. You guys have taken a lot of hits in the court of public opinion on the Max Crosby deal. >> I have not noticed. >> Are you concerned that that could impact the organization's reputation? And I don't believe we're going to talk to Steve here. How frustrated is he that the organization's sort of integrity is getting challenged? >> Yeah, I one I think it's a slow slow news cycle. I don't want to at all downplay the experience uh that uh that Max had coming that we all had. The Raiders, Ravens, Max, our locker room. As Eric said, uh, we were incredibly excited and just as equally, if not more, disappointed that we weren't able to pull off that transaction and bring Max, uh, to Baltimore. Uh, I'm not going to go too much deeper into that. To answer your specific question, we've got strong, long relationships across the league. We have emphasized the importance of doing things the right way. We'll continue to do that. And we understand that it is a headline story because of its profile and significance. Uh we believe, you know, our relationships to the extent that you need time to repair them, people understand who we are and what we're about. Our locker room understands that as well. Uh but when you have high-profile transactions like this and opportunities like this, it's unfortunate, but sometimes these things do happen. No fault of Max's certainly or ours or the Raiders. It's just kind of where it played out. because of how it played out. Are there changes in the whole the trade process, the new league gear process where you can agree to trades and it can't be announced that you like to see or is that there's no you don't think there's anything that this should spur? >> I think this is how it should be handled. I mean, I really do. Uh Jeff, the the we're not aiming for that result. >> But when you have a high stakes transaction like that, everybody needs to have understand kind of what conditions you're moving forward on. And you know, I won't say much more than that, but uh we understand we're disappointed it didn't go through, but we move on to the next to the next opportunity. Do you feel like it was even in that process where as you heard you said about the criticism that you feel has been maybe misconstrued or mischaracterized? >> Yeah, but we wouldn't get into that publicly honestly. Um and um we understand the need to report on, you know, these these high-profile cases and and certainly, but uh you know, as I said, we're going to trust ourselves and have a ton of respect for Max and treat all this with the right privacy and respect and dignity that it deserves. to follow up on on Jeff's question. Have there been any conversations, you know, regard to whether you think personally that that anything should change about how that process works with the two-day negotiating period and the start of the league year. Do you think the league is interested? Have they spoken to you at all about it? You know, just to see if they think anything should change, other team, other clubs, have other clubs, have you had any of those kind of conversations just about about the process, not >> Yeah. You know, I listen, I think there's steps that that teams take consistently. I think we just saw another team go through a very similar circumstance. This is not the first time it's going to happen. Uh it will not be the last. Uh so, you know, I think everybody wants to be prudent throughout processes and uh it's unfortunate and rare, especially in a high-profile case like this. Um but that's why the processes are in place. any news about international games? >> Not yet. Uh not yet. You know, we have two opportunities. The Falcons who are on our our list of scheduled opponents and the Cowboys are the two opportunities, but we have not been told they have not selected other than I think the Australia game. They have not selected opponents. >> I think I'm contractually obligated every year to ask about uniform changes. >> Oh, >> the the the annual inquiry. >> Yes. Uh we we as I've told you before, we'll we'll always update you when the time is right on the uniforms. So, and and you guys know, we're going to be last in line for the uh rivalry uniforms, which I think have we would start designing those in maybe a year. So, >> there was a tweet the other day that's that spurred some speculation further on on the uniforms. >> Just one. There's always a tweet, you know. It's always a tweet. Yeah. But the the the core of like helmets and that would not change as far as your >> in the hypothetical situation. >> You guys are good. >> You guys are good, man. You guys are good. >> Way to bring it back around. That's >> Yeah. You know, the process for designing uniforms is a lengthy one. Um so you you've got to go I think for rivalry we'll start like a year and a half in advance. Try to get through that process. So, we'll let you guys know when we're when when something's moving. >> Sasha, you're moving into the third phase of renovations or now. Um, but in general, you guys are kind of at the back end of when teams usually stay in their stadium. Have you guys started thinking about like longterm uh plans for? So, I think the renovations are a big part of that. Third phase, over $400 million invested, significant of those dollars from from us. Um, but thankful for the state. We're really excited to bring the entire project into fruition. Uh, starting this summer and this last phase may be the most significant and transformational because the the plaza really stands up and starts to take form. So, we are, as you know, through Steve, just really committed to learn from the lessons of the past in Baltimore Memorial Stadium, others to make sure we're delivering a first class fan and game day experience here in Baltimore. And Mnt Bank Stadium has been at the forefront of game day experiences and fan experiences as ranked, you know, throughout its history. This investment allows us, we believe, to stay right at the front of the pack despite the fact there have been other new builds. Part of that is because we have such an awesome fan base in the flock. But the other piece of that is because we put a lot of thought into the experience that every fan is going to have. So this plaza, the bump out on the north plaza above in the upper concourse, creation of new bathrooms, you guys get that question and comment a lot. I see them on on some of your stories. Where are the bathrooms? When are they coming? They're coming. 33% increase in the bathrooms. But the Northwest Plaza building will bring live entertainment accessible to every fan that comes in. Um, a ton of technology that we're investing in on the concourses, but also the plaza to modernize the stadium. And the nice thing, John, I think is that, you know, we have a stadium that has the bones to be able to continue invest 23 billion dollar tear down a new build. Uh so we're blessed that way and we're we're grateful for it. The complex is is rolling. Excited to see the O's roll out their first phase of renovations uh last week at on opening day and so we're really excited to deliver our stadium renovations here uh this summer completed. >> Another uh hot topic in the league is the 18 possibility of going to 18 games. >> Where would the Ravens stance be for that? I we'd leave that to the league and I think the union to negotiate. We're all watching it closely and you know that's always going to have to be a negotiation and compromise that works for both sides. We have a ton of respect for where we think the players interests are. I think collectively both sides see an opportunity, but we've got to work through what that what that's going to mean and how we make it work. >> Another thing that could be changing the league level is starting to see the talk about renegotiating the TV deals that could obviously change the economics of the league and the game greatly. Are you starting to sort of >> put some variables into your future planning in an organizational level or is it too soon for this? >> Too soon for this for us at an organizational level. The league does a great job of two things. One, keeping us apprised of their plans and the work that they're putting in on the media side. Secondly, you know, I give a lot of credit to Roger and his team, uh, Hans, who's now running that group is to stay on the front edge of, you know, the innovations, the technologies that need to happen. Our fan base has remained very strong. where they find the games or where we find them to deliver games to them has been disrupted quite a bit. And I think when I first got here, you all were asking me questions about the Thursday night package on Prime and you know, some of those things have become normalized now. But the league has done a nice job of monitoring and structuring our media contracts and are finding new partners and technology streamers uh to deliver our game to where our fans are. um particularly I think important for us as we try to find younger fans um and how they consume our our content in in our live games. >> Speaking of the the league, I think it was a couple years ago that you guys your pat so to speak for the draft in Baltimore and where is that process at with you guys? >> Yeah, we're still in communications, active communication with the league. These are rolling processes where the league gets a chance to know the local market. Uh we're very much uh working with our public civic partners, Visit Baltimore, the city of Baltimore, the state, but also um in communication with the league. And I think we're going to have we already have and I think we're going to continue to have really strong prospects bringing the draft, but until that happens, um you know, we'll be working at it very hard. >> And the idea would be to utilize the stadium or some portion of it. That's TBD. But another good good shot at trying to get me to roll out our plans before we get a get a chance to really really finalize. We know. But in all seriousness, I think um there's a lot of assets in and around Baltimore that make it tremendously unique. The harbor, the development around we have one of the most unique sports complex with a baseball stadium and uh a football stadium that that you can see each other, you know, from from our parking lots and from our upper decks uh concourses. So there's a lot of opportunity for us to do some really creative things and of course the city has two beautiful massive parks. You've seen those utilized different places. Uh so there's a lot of opportunity and we are exploring all of those uh potential sites. >> Continuing the draft conversation. Um how much do you guys hope the roughly match that you are will help you guys? I think it's a great opportunity for us to showcase as was the Messi game, right? That the Mid-Atlantic, Baltimore in particular, Maryland has a very, very strong appetite for all kinds of sport. Uh, our team enjoys tremendous support from our fan base. They are also hungry European football, soccer, global football, um, rugby and and other sports. We've I think we've talked about why are the stadium renovations important? There's a lot of reasons they're important. One of the reasons is we want the stadium Steve's commitment to being downtown Baltimore to drive more people, fan activity downtown Baltimore. And you all know we have six nights of events uh that are coming to Mnt Bank outside of Ravens games this year. So that's incredibly important for us to deliver on that objective that we set with the state when we renovated. And I think the international match puts us on a global scale a little bit like the AFC Championship did where you know just there's so many people around the world and around the country watching South Africa, New Zealand, you can't find a more significant kind of international iconic matchup. Uh so credit to our teams Brad Down who went out and hunted that opportunity and brought it back to our stadium. Rich Tomio who's here uh as well has done a tremendous job at attracting global international events. Mnt Bank Stadium in Baltimore. >> Have you guys decided on ticket prices? Is there going to be an increase this year? >> We have uh not decided on that yet. Um, so we will announce that at the right time. Um, Jeff, so sorry about that. But yeah, >> Sasha, this off season has done a lot for the organization overall. >> Yeah, lot of change >> professionally and personally. What have you kind of learned about yourself dealing with the the different change? Yeah, it's been the first time we've had really significant change in almost two decades, right? And Steve talked about this. We committed to avoid being an organization that relies on change to get where we think there's a lot of value to making finding good people, committing to them, pushing through adversity. And so I think this is the first opportunity for Eric at the helm, myself to go through a coaching search and work together with Steve, with Azie, with with Dick at points as well through that process. I think we worked well together. Um, and there were others involved certainly, but I think it was an important opportunity for us to bring all of our unique experiences and and expertise to a coaching search. But there was more than that. You know, with every coaching search, a lot comes. You guys seen we've hired some new people, structured things a little bit differently. So, it's a great opportunity for us to step back, look at the way we've done things for the better part of the last two decades, uh, and make some changes, move forward that we think are going to position us as well as possible. Most importantly, I think we worked really well together through change, adversity, uh, and opportunity. >> Sasha, young, not to ask you a question that I know you're probably not going to answer, but uh, Lamar, not so much on the contract negotiation stuff. Eric's talked about that, but what have you, I guess, seen um in this process? You know, they Eric's talked about a little bit, Jesse, as well in terms of Lamar's involvement in the process when you guys were hiring uh the coach and what have you seen, I guess, from the engagement standpoint and and what level of confidence do you guys have that will have an extension? Yeah, Lamar's, you know, at a point in his career where he's seen so much. So, we value his opinion tremendously. He knows and has shaped and led our organization. And so, it was great to have his involvement. You guys talked to Jess about his interaction with him through his his process. Same with Eric. uh he and Lamar have been in contact and so you know it's nice to have that engagement and I think there's just a tremendous amount of respect for what he brings to the table and what we're going to be able to do together. I'll defer all the as you guys know uh no different than when Dick was here. I'll defer all the contract discussions out of respect for Lamar but also the organization to Eric and he'll be able to answer those. your team being recognized by their peers across the league. Um I'm curious what does that mean to you and how do they help you at all? >> Yeah, so Eric Oz the organization have done a great job at positioning us to try to find competitive advantage. One area that I think that's been um we don't publicize much uh but is in the area of just kind of football operation intelligence. We also have stood up a group on the business side for business intelligence that works separately from that. Uh so we're grateful to have in this era of just the the dynamic power value of having innovation, technology, data available to help us make great decisions. Uh and to have I think leadership on both sides of organization that really invests and believes in process and information so that we can make the best possible decisions. The big decisions we're making, we needed to get them right. And uh I think our our team top to bottom is really strong on both sides of the organization. >> Is that it? >> One more on >> Obviously with respect to to privacy in NAB and Eric has talked about that and sort of leaving it up to him to address that. Is there um I guess where would you gauge the organization's um optimism sense of where things are at timeline of how you know things will develop as we get toward the offseason program here couple weeks at >> TBD be too early to to appine or express any optimism or pessimism? Don't read into it one way or the other. uh you know he's going to have to get himself to a point uh you know here where you know he and Eric are I'm sure going to have plenty of conversation until that time and and even when that time comes I'll let Eric comment but um I don't take it as pessimism or optimism it's just got to go through the process

title: GM George Paton on Broncos' WR corps after Waddle trade: 'We really like our room'
text: It's good to be here. Good to be in the weather. Uh don't get to experience it much um as we meet, you know, every day and then we get back Wednesday and we have draft meetings. So, pretty exciting stuff. Uh happy to take your questions. >> George, can you just walk us through the the Waddle deal and how it came over? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, we had an interest at the trade deadline. I think everyone knows that. Um it didn't get very far then. Um but we still like the player a lot. Uh got through our off-season process with our roster and then free agent meetings and and uh and really it was just kind of still out there. You know, at the combine we hadn't talked yet. And then when we got back to the combine, uh reached out um to John Eric and then it kind of started from there and and obviously did a lot of work on him. All the coaches did, scouts. Um we'd done a lot of work at the trade deadline. Um we felt like we knew the player well. We knew the person um even better. And so feel really good about the trade. George, what what does he bring to this team? Well, he's one of the more ex- you know, explosive playmakers in the league first and foremost. Um great makeup, great competitor. He'll fit in well with our room. Uh we really like our room. I've said that uh on a number of, you know, Courtland and Pat Bryant and Troy and and Mimsy. So, we have a great room and he just upgrades or he just helps the room and uh opens up the run game. He'll open it up for the other receivers. Um so, we think he'll fit in well with the group. >> George, how does this kind of change your draft strategy? I mean, obviously don't have the first round or lower rounder. How does that all affect Well, obviously we're focused on the 30 in the second. You know, we've been fortunately been there before. I think two different times and so we have a good feel for that and we can we can hone in. Doesn't mean we won't trade up at some point, but we'll have a really good feel for, you know, the 62nd pick or whatever we're picking. You know, we took a Mims at 64, you know, Bonitto 64. We have a pretty Harvey maybe 60, I think. So, we have a pretty good feel um you know, of that realm. George, when you say you like the room, is there any consideration now to to moving any pieces that you have in the receiver >> No, we really like those pieces and they're all going to help us. They've they've all helped us up to now. I'm going a little Jordan and and Bandy. I mean, we we really like we're seven eight deep. We really like it and so why would we you know, build up this room then then trade someone right now? When you have a when when you when you're talking about dealing a first round pick and plus obviously that's that's steep or is a lot. So, when you like just what goes into that conversation and does the caliber of the class or sort of what it looks like at 30, Well, you do look at that. You look at the caliber of the free agent class. You look at the caliber of the draft class. Who can we get at 30 within the draft class? [music] Then you factor in the cap and the finances, you know, not just this year but down the road. The fact that he's 27 years old, uh the fact that it was 30, it wasn't 16. Uh we compared it to all the other trades the last 10 years of with a first round pick and and the the value we felt, you know, was 26. That's the the value we we gave him and and so you look into all that when you make a trade like this. I mean, I no one loves picks more than me. So, that that's hard and I've probably traded too many, god darn it, but uh but I think it's worked out. >> George, how how close were you to getting a deal done at the trade deadline? You mentioned that there I wouldn't say it was real close, you know, I think uh they kind of stuck to their guns. I give them a lot of credit um and and and really John Eric, you know, and first time GM, I mean, total pro the way he handled everything. Um so, it worked out. >> Was there anything that kind kind of changing your thinking in terms of sacrificing draft capital between late October and this point based on >> You know, you kind of know where you we you know, we know it's 30 now, you know, in in in late October you know, we didn't know where it would be. We again, we were healthy at receiver. You know, we we we were unhealthy towards the end of the season and so we liked our group. We I mean, we were on a win streak, you know, we were we were rolling pretty good and the and it was high. I mean, they were asking a lot at that time and then the more you think about it, the more you go through all your different models, like I said, cap and and draft picks, who's available in the draft, free agency, all that. Um who could really help us, you know, our team. It it had to be a unique circumstance for us to do this to make a trade like this and we just felt this was too unique to pass up. >> George, could you take us through your the conversation with PS2 when you let him know that his uh college roommate was coming back? >> Well, I he knew. Like I called him um and I talked to Pat about him a lot at the trade at the trade deadline. I didn't talk to him before this and um but I did call him, attempted to get a hold of him and he called me right back. I mean, he was he was screaming. He was very happy. That's his guy as you know. In free agency, can you talk about prioritizing your own guys Right. >> lot of the outside? Well, I mean, uh yep and I think you kept tally. How what do we have? We got the first tally. >> it was 17. >> 17. We like our players. I mean, that was the plan. We we compare all our players to what's there in free agency and our guys favored, you know, where they were pretty high and then we won a lot of games with these guys. They fit the culture and not everyone does. Hard working good I mean, you're talking Singleton and Strnad and JK Dobbins. They really changed the landscape of our offense and Trout and and those type of guys. And then you kind of look it's just an extension of what we've done over the last year and a half. You know, we had 10 extensions and these are some of the best players in the league. Surtain, Meinerz, Bonitto, Zach Allen, Roach. I mean, Court, Bolles, all these guys. And so, you can't do that and then make a big splash like some of these teams do. And so, we feel really good with what we accomplished in free agency. We filled a lot of needs with good players that we know and yet we had flexibility to go make a trade. And so, if we didn't if we just jumped out and made a big splash to trade, we wouldn't been able to make the trade. Can you specifically address the decision at inside linebacker holding on to Singleton and Strnad and then letting Greenlaw go? Well, we just we I mean, Singleton and Strnad are just really good players and Dre we couldn't keep the three of them. Uh Dre helped us win, you know, a bunch of games. He helped our culture. We wish him the best, but uh we're really happy to have Strnad and Singleton. With JK, kind of how do you kind of balance like what he brought versus also the fact that unfortunately he's landed on IR each year? No, you're right. It's it's a tough balance, but um he's 27 years old. He's completely healthy now. Um that injury was kind of a it was a hip drop, you know, it was a freak. His body didn't break down. He could have played in the Super Bowl. Um this guy from the minute he walked in our building changed it. And so, it's like you know, we just didn't want to let him leave. You know, he meant too much to the building. He's a he was a top four rusher in the league when he got hurt. Um let's sign him back. You know, he meant too much to this team. George, I think last year you signed him for over 84% on roster retention. It was the number one in the league. And I'd be willing to bet you got to be right around there if not higher. What I think How unique is that and what's that kind of say about where y'all are? >> Yeah, I haven't done the studies on that. I know it's probably pretty unique, you know, especially this year. I think uh it's not for everyone what what we're doing, you know, in the culture and and man, the guys we have, you know, really fit it. Um it just it's kind of worked out that way, you know, um it's hard to get deals done in free agency. We're able to get deals done with our guys and we're glad to have them here. Time for a few more for George. With with JK though, just the the injury history, are you comfortable with the backs that you have there? Are you looking We are. We like the we like the backs. Um um RJ's just going to keep getting better. What do you have? 12 touchdowns? Explosive play I mean, explosive receiver out of the backfield. Matchup problem. He's going to get better as a runner. He got better as the year went on. Then you got Badey, you got Jaleel. Uh we got Cody Schrader we like. We're going to be looking in the draft. We're going to be looking after the draft. We're always looking. I mean, we didn't sign JK till what? May or June last year. So, we feel good with where we're at right now. I mean, last year at this time we didn't have JK and we didn't have RJ and you know, we were we were we were okay, you know. So, we'll we're going to be fine. Tiden, do you feel How do you kind of reset from last year and then start over? Obviously made it all the way to AFC Championship. >> Yeah. Kind of go all the way back to square one like Sean talks about. How difficult is is that to do? It's not difficult at all. It's what we do. We start over and uh and it starts the day after the season as you get through all your evaluations and free agency and the draft and then once you get in the off-season program, I mean, you start over and the players know that and it's it's you just don't show up with a you know, 14 14 wins. You know, you got to start over and and Sean obviously will emphasize that. As you're going through the the sort of first opening days of free agency, how much once JFM signed the deal in Tennessee, like how much does the idea of having a pretty good comp pick in 27 sort of factor into what you do you know, down >> Yeah, it does. I mean, it doesn't dictate what kind of what we're doing, but we obviously know it's there. We we got, you know, two compensatory picks this year. Uh Mr. Irrelevant, Pat's really happy about that all in the media. And then we have Mr. Irrelevant runner up. So, it'll be cool. He'll be working a lot after the draft. And then next year we're you know, we should get the four and maybe a seven. That's what you That's what you want to get to. It took us a while to get here, you know, where we can get compensatory picks and and you see other teams do it and and I'm I'm I like that we're doing it. George, you talk about talk talk about talk about those picks, but how valuable can those chips be especially you're negotiating with guys in round seven and maybe you don't know if you can get them as undrafted guys. >> It's great. It's great because you may not be able to get a guy he's he's, you know, the price gets higher sometimes than the picks, you know, um in the free agent world. It's crazy the chaos and and so if we're not going to get a guy, we you know, that happened with Jonathan Cooper, believe it or not. He's going to go to Jacksonville with Urban Meyer. Let's just take him, you know, rather let him walk out and we took him. And so, those sevens, I mean, I mean, we got Valery in the seventh, we got Cooper in the seventh. I mean, there's probably more, but um they're very I mean, all those picks are important. George, what kind of Bo's reaction is to adding a playmaker like Waddle and his I mean, yeah, I wasn't with him when he found out, but he was pretty excited when I walked down to the training room. He was excited. Obviously went to dinner with all of us. Um you know, Bo both I think thinks he's kind of a quasi GM sometimes and uh sometimes he's right, sometimes he's wrong.
